Preposition + Ing
Every time you find a preposition and a verb or action together in a sentence, the verb must be a gerund, that is, the termination -ing.

First of all, you need to understand that prepositions are words that you use to indicate the relationships between different words in a sentence. For example, in, at, with, for, about, or of, among many others.

When a verb comes after a preposition, you need to add the termination -ing. It means that in a sentence if you have a preposition, the verb that goes after it takes the –ing form.

Take into consideration that the preposition “to” most of times represents the infinitive form of a verb rather than the preposition.

For example, the verb like does not have a preposition; therefore you can say:

I like to use HTML instead of CSS.

 On the other hand, the verb confess always goes with the preposition to, that is, confess to.

He confessed to having no idea about how HTML worked.

 Therefore, a common structure where you could find a preposition + gerund is as follows: 

(Subject) + Main verb + Preposition + Action (gerund) + complement.

 For example:

  • Before creating a webpage, you need to learn basic concepts of HTML.
  • She convinced me of using HTML5 instead of CSS to design the website for the company.

The History of the World Wide Web and HTML
The creation of the World Wide Web is often confused with the creation of the internet, but they are different. Let’s check some historical data.

The World Wide Web (www) is a global network that works on the internet platform. The invention of the www dates back to 1980. However, a decade after the invention of the internet, Tim Berners-Lee, an independent worker at the European Organization for Nuclear Research ,CERN, developed ENQUIRES (a database that was able to interact with the hypertext). With this new prototype, every new page they created had to be linked to an existing page.

In 1984, Berners-Lee returned to CERN and realized that around the world scientists needed to share information through their computers, but there was a limitation to make this to happen, as software and hardware were very different one another.

By 1989, he wrote a first proposal for the development of the www, but that generated little interest in the organization. Later that year, he worked with Robert Cailliau to develop the necessary tools for creating the www. Those tools were: the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP); the first browser, WorldWideWeb, that later changed to Nexus; the first application server; and the hypertext markup language (HTML). All of them allowed the development of web pages that used a unified language.

In 1991, Berners-Lee wrote 18 elements that included an earlier design of HTML.

By 1992, several scientific departments of universities and laboratories around the world adopted the www. The first websites showed consulting pages and updated lists. On the other hand, the first stable web browser appeared in 1993, Mosaic, and in 1994, Robert Cailliau organized the first international conference of the WWW at CERN. Since that moment on, many browsers started to appear, some of them are no longer there, like Netscape, but there are some other browsers that still there, such as E-explorer or Mozilla. Nowadays, web browsers not only support html, but CSS and many other languages such as Java, JavaScript, and more.

Ms. Lopez: In order to continue with the topic of how to create a website, we need to clarify some key concepts that will make our life easier at the moment of creating our webpages. I’m talking, of course, about HTML and the web. Who can tell me the relationship between those ones?
Jeffery: Well, Ms. Lopez, I might be wrong, but I think they must have a close relationship, as one works inside the other. I mean, HTML works inside the web, or world wide web, as a tool for displaying websites and webpages.
Ms. Lopez: Well done, Jeffery. You are right about that one, their main relation is that we use html inside the web for presenting the information we have on our websites. But, do you know how it works?

Jeffery: Well, that I don’t know.
Ms. Lopez: Ok, as you all know, HTML is a hypertext markup language, that is, a special language we, as developers, use to tell the web browser how to display the information we have. However, such information has a hidden code that we write inside some tags. Thus, the main components you need to learn by hearth before writing code with html are: syntax, tags, and of course, the text editor.

Jeffery: Sorry, Ms. Lopez. Could you give us some examples of them?
Ms. Lopez: Of course; for example, the first one: when developing a webpage, you need to be good at writing code in html language, I mean, you need to manage the syntax of the language. Similarly, you have to know how to use the tags, as there are containers and empty tags. The first ones are for containing the whole code, and the empty ones are for giving specific instructions without code in them, an example being the break one. Finally, you need to write the code inside the tags with the proper syntax in a text editor, that is, the Notepad in windows or TextEdit in MAC. Anyway, there are more versions of HTML, in fact, the latest one is HTML5, but before working with it, you need to learn the ropes by reading about HTML.
